solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get angry when you see that is being such an animal exterminator

definitions.text: Get angry when you see that is being such an animal exterminator

parts.words: Get angry when you see that is being such an animal exterminator
parts.note: the clue pictures someone who flies into a fury at the sight of a certain rodent, and whose job is to deal with that very creature

explanation.surface: Someone's temper flares at the sight of a pest, which is just as well given their trade.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate wordplay: 'that' points to the animal you get angry at seeing, and 'such an animal exterminator' asks for a person who catches that very animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest controller who traps rodents is the trade name described, an exterminator of one kind of animal.

clue.text: Bad, being stranded?

definitions.meaning: informal British sense: poor in quality or a bit unwell
whimsically, made of strands like a cord or cable

explanation.surface: Things are looking poor for someone left stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: 'stranded' usually means marooned, but here it means made of strands, like rope.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for shoddy or off-colour, and literally it describes something stringy or cord-like.

clue.text: Versed in books no end? You must get hold of that American author

indicators.note: one word must grip another, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: thou is the old form of you

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for well-read is cut off

parts.note: someone versed in books is well read, so read

explanation.surface: A reader is told that, to know their books thoroughly, they must take up a certain American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' leaves REA; 'must get hold of' says the archaic pronoun wraps it, and 'that' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, who wrote Walden, is a celebrated nineteenth-century writer from Massachusetts.

clue.text: Ex-President right and judicious or diverging from normality?

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a former US President
judicious means sensible or reasonable, so rational

explanation.surface: A question whether a former president was principled and wise or rather eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deviating from the usual pattern is the adjective formed from aberration, a departure from what is normal.

clue.text: Most important shift, EEC becoming something else

indicators.note: the letters change into a different arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A vital change of direction for the old European Economic Community as it turns into another body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming something else' rearranges the eight letters of SHIFT and EEC; the EEC really did become the EU, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief means principal, and this rare superlative form means the most principal or foremost of all.

clue.text: Painting displayed in the Louvre's season shows Parisian star

indicators.note: a painting shown inside a gallery, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Louvre is in Paris, so the season is in French: ete, summer
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: An exhibition at the Louvre during a particular season features a French celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Mentioning the Louvre means the season must be named in French; 'displayed in' signals the container, and 'shows' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a star, also used for a principal ballet dancer, is what a Parisian would call one.

clue.text: Any number taken in by wicked gang

indicators.note: the number is absorbed inside the next word

parts.note: wicked means bad
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Plenty of people have been lured into an evil gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang or group of people banded together, as in a band of robbers.

clue.text: A servant collects an allowance for looking after children?

definitions.note: the question mark admits this is a fanciful gloss on a royal provision for younger offspring

indicators.note: the servant gathers the following word into himself

parts.note: a page is a young servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A domestic servant picks up some extra money for childminding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' signals the container. The definition whimsically reads the provision made historically for younger royal children.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an endowment of land or income granted to younger sons of royalty, hence a provision for children.

clue.text: Rulers cheat, endlessly threatening society

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: minatory means menacing or threatening

explanation.surface: Those in power swindle the people while the whole of society is under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims MINATORY, a formal word for menacing, to MINATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who dominate others are their masters or overlords, so rulers in a broad sense.

clue.text: No amateur toff leading soldiers, one held to be a forefather

indicators.note: the toff goes in front of the soldiers

parts.note: someone who is not an amateur is a professional, a pro

indicators.note: the number one is gripped inside the word for the toff

parts.note: a toff is a gentleman, a gent
I is the Roman numeral one
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A professional aristocrat at the head of a troop is thought to be someone's ancestor.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for an upper-class man; 'held' and 'leading' set the order, and 'to be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor from whom a line descends, the originator of a family, is a forefather.

clue.text: Contest that has millions excited

parts.note: a war is a contest or struggle
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A competition with huge sums at stake has people thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings described as heated or ardent are excited ones, as in a lively or animated debate.

clue.text: Change takes bit of time in tricky atmosphere

indicators.note: the short time sits inside the jumbled letters
a tricky situation is a confused one, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Things alter when a moment is spent in a difficult mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'takes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to transform completely, as a caterpillar does into a butterfly, so to change.

clue.text: Sport a flower in the north

definitions.meaning: to sport clothes is to have them on
a flower is something that flows, a river; this one runs through Durham in northern England

explanation.surface: Wear a bloom from up north in your buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick for a river (something that flows), not a bloom; this river flows through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a hat is to have it on, and the river through Durham carries the same name.

clue.text: Wand perhaps giving deceptive appearance

parts.note: the answer read as instructions says a false form of a word, and a scrambled version of that word gives wand

explanation.surface: A magic wand might create an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'false' as an anagram signal applied to DAWN gives WAND, one possible ('perhaps') result.
explanation.definitionFit: A light before true daybreak, and figuratively any promising sign that proves illusory, is a misleading appearance.

clue.text: Awkward drives around country — one moves through water

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the country
awkward suggests the letters are clumsily out of place

parts.note: taken as written
Cuba is a Caribbean country

explanation.surface: Poor driving around a Caribbean island, while someone else swims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' gives SDIVER, which 'around' wraps about the island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater swimmer with breathing apparatus is someone who moves through the sea.

clue.text: Good manners in group game suffering setback — get reticent about that

indicators.note: the reticent word goes around the rest

parts.note: coy means shy or reticent

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a group
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Polite behaviour in a team game that has gone badly: say nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' gives URTES and 'about' wraps the shy word around it; 'get' and 'that' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Politeness and respectful consideration for others amount to good manners.

clue.text: Conspicuous church plate on middle of altar

parts.note: a paten is the plate holding the bread at the Eucharist

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A noticeable piece of communion plate is set in the centre of the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the T from ALTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means obvious or evident, as in a patent lie, so conspicuous.

clue.text: Doctor keeps strange times, creating row at home

indicators.note: the doctor holds the following letters inside

parts.note: doc is a doctor

indicators.note: strange signals the letters in an odd order

explanation.surface: A medic with odd hours causes rows in the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' gives MESTI, which 'keeps' places inside. In British slang the answer as a noun means a household quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a quarrel between partners or family members, such as police might be called to.

clue.text: See leader dance, having drunk his rum

indicators.note: the dance swallows the letters

parts.note: a bop is a dance

indicators.note: rum means odd, so the word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A dance leader who has had a drink of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but means strange, giving ISH, which 'having drunk' puts inside the dance. A see is a diocese, so its leader is its senior cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a diocese, or see, is the senior clergyman who oversees it.

clue.text: Thus a man on board may get very wet

parts.note: so means thus
the king is a chessman on the board

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck might get drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a ship's deck, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Drenched or wet through, as in a soaking towel, is very wet.

clue.text: One helping animal needing to get round by foreign river

parts.note: a dog is an animal
O is round in shape
the Oder flows between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A rescuer of an animal needs to get it around a river on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-meaning person who tries to help others, often officiously, is a helper.

clue.text: Great shot has you almost mute at first

indicators.note: the shortened word comes in front
the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to mute a sound is to deaden it
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A superb marksman leaves someone almost silent at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the verb by one letter, and 'at first' puts it in front; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert marksman who rarely misses, so an excellent shot.

clue.text: Meticulousness of person working on ship being reported

indicators.note: reported speech, so the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: a rigger works on a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: A sailor's thoroughness is the subject of a report.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded final R, the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict precision and thoroughness in method is meticulousness.

clue.text: For new set-up, it's a dream colour

indicators.note: the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A designer exclaims that the shade chosen for a refit is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For new set-up' rearranges IT'S A DREAM. 'colour' looks like a noun but is the verb: to exaggerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour a story is to embellish or exaggerate it, making it more theatrical.

clue.text: Sport to make a profit — pounds coming in

indicators.note: the pounds enter the middle of the profit word

parts.note: a venture that pays makes money
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A sporting venture becomes lucrative once money arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation and games are play, and to sport is to frolic.

clue.text: Some tacky attempt to make money abroad

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheap effort to get rich overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'to make', but the answer is a noun, so 'to make' is a link and 'money abroad' alone defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Myanmar is a foreign unit of money.

clue.text: Very short story brought back for screen

parts.note: V is the short form of very

indicators.note: the word is returned the other way round

parts.note: a story is a lie

explanation.surface: A brief tale is revived for the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short' looks like a description of the story but means V, the abbreviation; 'brought back' turns LIE into EIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin covering that conceals, as in drawing a veil over something, is a screen.

clue.text: Soldier upset by gory moment

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fighting man is distressed by a bloody incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges GORY MOMENT; 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Montgomery was the British commander victorious at El Alamein, a famous soldier.

clue.text: Jelly set about establishing one form of music

indicators.note: turned about means reversed

parts.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: A jelly is left to set before someone composes a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like describing a jelly setting, but it reverses AGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian classical melodic pattern on which improvisation is based is a musical form.

clue.text: To get race trophy involves torture still

indicators.note: the trophy wraps itself around the rest

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races
the rack is an instrument of torture
even means still, as in even more

explanation.surface: Winning a cup for a race still requires agony.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races; 'involves' signals the container, and 'To get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Any running contest held on a track, such as a sprint or relay, is a race.
